c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: Renewal of Wayne County Zoological Authority Millage in Support of the Detroit Zoo
c.q:
In 2008 and 2016, pursuant to Public Act 49 of 2008, Wayne County voters renewed a 10-year property tax millage to fund zoological services through the Wayne County Zoological

Authority, supporting animal care for more than 2,000 animals and 200 species, educational and senior programs, and facility maintenance at the Detroit Zoo.

To continue providing these services, the Authority seeks to renew and restore the millage to the original voter-approved rate of 0.10 mill (10 cents per $1,000 of taxable value). This

proposal would renew the millage at 0.0982 mill and restore the remaining 0.0018 mill that was reduced due to required rollback, for a total authorized rate of 0.10 mill on taxable real and personal property for ten (10) years.

If approved, the millage rate would be unchanged from those approved by voters in 2008 and 2016. Funds will be disbursed to the Authority and transferred to the Detroit Zoo as permitted by law. All funds are subject to annual independent audits. It is estimated that $6,145,462 will be collected in the first year.

Ballot Question:

Do you approve the renewal and restoration of the levy of 0.10 mill on all taxable property in Wayne County for a period of ten (10) years, from 2028 through 2037?

c.title: Southeast Michigan Public Historical Museum Authority Millage Proposal
c.q:
The Southeast Michigan Public Historical Museum Authority (“Authority”) is a joint authority established by Wayne and Oakland Counties (“Counties”) pursuant to Michigan Public Act 321 of the Public Acts of 2000, as amended, and was formed to support the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History, Detroit Historical Museum, Dossin Great Lakes Museum, and other public historical museums located in Wayne and Oakland Counties (“Historical Museums”) that provide historical museum services for students, residents and visitors of the Counties. The law allows the Authority to seek authorization from the electors in each of the Counties to levy a tax of 0.2 mill (20 cents per $1,000 of taxable value) on taxable property to provide revenue for Historical Museums.

It is estimated that if approved and levied on taxable property located within Wayne County, this new millage would generate approximately $12,219,200 in 2026.

In addition to supporting the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History, Detroit Historical Museum, and Dossin Great Lakes Museum, 15% of revenues received by the Authority from taxable property in Wayne County, after Authority administrative expenses, will be disbursed to the County of Wayne for the purposes of supporting Historical Museums in Wayne County.

Shall a 0.2 mill tax on all taxable property located within Wayne County be imposed by the Authority for a period of ten (10) years, being years 2026 through 2035, inclusive, to provide historical museum services for the benefit of the residents of the Counties?

c.title: School District of the City of Wyandotte Operating Millage Proposal
c.q:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.

Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in School District of the City of Wyandotte, Wayne County, Michigan, be increased by 1.6547 mills ($1.6547 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 9 years, 2027 to 2035, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $0 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?

c.title: Headlee Operating Millage Restoration for Transportation Infrastructure
c.q:
Shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be imposed upon taxable property in the City of Rockwood be increased by restoring 1.9055 mills ($1.9055 per $1,000 of taxable value) of the City's previously reduced charter-authorized operating tax levy as a new additional millage for a period of ten years, 2026 through 2035, inclusive, thereby increasing the City's maximum authorized operating tax levy from 15.9814 mills to 17.8869 mills, with all revenue generated from the restored 1.9055 mills to be used exclusively for the repair, maintenance, preservation, and improvement of public roads, streets, bridges, sidewalks, and other transportation infrastructure?

If approved and levied, this restoration is estimated to raise approximately $102,761.42 in 2026, the first year of the levy.

c.title: City of Grosse Pointe Park
c.q:
This millage proposal would allow the City of Grosse Pointe Park to levy 0.65 Mill for the purpose of, maintaining, preserving, repairing, replacing, and extending the useful life of the parks and recreation facilities located within the City of Grosse Pointe Park.

Shall the City of Grosse Pointe Park, Wayne County, Michigan, increase the limitation on the total amount of general ad valorem taxes which may be imposed for all purposes in Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, as amended, by 0.65 Mill ($0.65 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for a period of seven (7) years (2027 through 2033, inclusive), which would provide an estimated revenue of $562,000.00 in its first year if approved and levied, for the purpose of, maintaining, preserving, repairing, replacing, improving, upgrading, and extending the useful life of the parks and recreation facilities located within the City of Grosse Pointe Park, of which a portion will be disbursed to the City of Grosse Pointe Park Downtown Development Authority and the City of Grosse Pointe Park Tax Increment Financing Authority. Should the proposed millage be approved?

c.title: Special Assessment for Police and Fire Departments
c.q: Should the City of Grosse Pointe raise money to partially equip, maintain, and operate the City Police and Fire Departments (Public Safety) by annual special assessment levies of up to 1.25 mills ($1.25 per $1,000 of taxable value) on all real property in the City that is not exempt from property taxes, for a period of four (4) years with the levies to be from 2026 to 2029 to provide funding for the 2027 to 2030 calendar years? If approved and fully levied in December 2026, the estimated revenue from this special assessment collected in the first year would be approximately $613,750.00.

c.title: City of Gibraltar
c.q: Shall the City of Gibraltar, County of Wayne, Michigan, be authorized to levy a new additional millage in an amount not to exceed 3.5 mills ($3.50 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) on all taxable real and personal property in the City, for a period of five (5) years, 2027 through 2031, inclusive, for the purpose of funding police, fire, and emergency (public safety) services, including related personnel, benefits, equipment, apparatus, and capital replacement? If approved and levied in full, this millage is estimated to raise approximately $672,281.68 for the City in the first calendar year of the levy (2027). A portion of the revenue collected may be captured by and disbursed to the City of Gibraltar Downtown Development Authority.

c.title: Sumpter Township
c.q:
Shall Sumpter Township impose a levy up to 5 mills ($5.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for 4

years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, for police protection, operations, and maintenance of the Sumpter Township police department, which 5 mills levy will raise an estimated $2,428,884 in the

first year the millage is levied?

c.title: City of Riverview Bond Proposal
c.q: Shall the City of Riverview, County of Wayne, Michigan, borrow the principal sum of not to exceed Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds, in one or more series, payable in not to exceed ten (10) years from the date of issue of each series, for the purpose of paying the cost to acquire, construct, furnish and equip road improvements throughout the city, including water main replacements, including interests in land, necessary rights-of-way and appurtenances and attachments thereto? If approved, the estimated millage to be levied in 2027 is 2.5211 mills ($2.5211 per $1,000 of taxable value) and the estimated simple average annual millage rate required to retire the bonds is 2.5229 mills ($2.5229 per $1,000 of taxable value).

c.title: City of Riverview Ballot Proposal
c.q: Shall the City of Riverview be authorized to publicly sell a portion of the City of Riverview’s Highlands Golf Course property, previously dedicated for recreational purposes, to the highest qualified bidder subject to City Council’s approval, for the development of a Community Park and approximately 400 Residential Housing Units? The property to be sold is located within the Riverview Highlands Golf Course and consists of not to exceed 80 acres of land (out of a total of approximately of 248.5 acres), adjacent to and west of the Forest Subdivision and north of King Road.

c.title: Riverview Community School District
c.q:
Shall Riverview Community School District, Wayne County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Thirty Million Dollars ($30,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:

erecting and remodeling school buildings, facilities and additions to school buildings and facilities; equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and refurnishing school buildings and facilities; purchasing school buses; acquiring and installing instructional technology; and preparing, developing, improving and equipping athletic fields, play fields, playgrounds, structures, facilities and sites?

The following is for informational purposes only:

The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 1.21 mills ($1.21 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a 0.00 mills net increase over the prior year’s levy. The maximum number of years the bonds of any series may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is twenty-five (25) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 2.72 mills ($2.72 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).

(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)

c.title: Millage Renewal Request for the
c.pre: City of Inkster Parks & Recreation which includes Senior Citizens and Youth Services
c.q:
Shall the City of Inkster, Wayne County, Michigan be authorized and empowered to levy a general valorem property tax which in any one year shall not exceed 2.0 mills (2.0 mills per $1,000.00 of State Equalized Valuation for ten (10) years, 2027 to 2036?

The continuation of the dedicated Millage for Parks and Recreation Operations, which include Youth and Senior Programs, is up to 2.0 mills. It has been determined that up to 2.0 mills is necessary to operate these programs and to continue the current level of service. General Fund dollars are not available to support these programs. The average cost to a homeowner is estimated to be $54 and would generate an estimated $580,000 if the maximum allowable millage is levied.

c.title: Millage Renewal Request
c.pre: for the City of Inkster Senior Services Operations
c.q:
Shall the City of Inkster, Wayne County, Michigan be authorized and empowered to levy a general valorem property tax which in any one year shall not exceed 1.0 mills (1.0 mills per $1,000.00 of State Equalized Valuation for ten (10) years, 2027 to 2036?

The continuation of the dedicated Millage for Senior Services Operations is up to 1.0 mills. It has been determined that up to 1.0 mills is necessary to operate this program and to continue the current level of service. General Fund dollars are not available to support these programs. The average cost to a homeowner is estimated to be $27 and would generate an estimated $290,000 if the maximum allowable amount is levied in any year.

c.title: Romulus Community Schools
c.q:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy millage previously authorized to be levied on all property, except property exempted by law and renews hold harmless millage that expired with the 2026 tax levy.

Shall the total limitation on the hold harmless mills used for operating purposes which may be assessed against all property, except property exempted by law, in Romulus Community Schools, Wayne County, Michigan, be increased by 2.5 mills ($2.50 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 10 years, 2027 to 2036, inclusive; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect from hold harmless taxes authorized herein if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $745,254 (this is a renewal of previously authorized millage that expired with the 2026 tax levy)?

c.title: City of Southgate
c.pre: Charter Amendment to Remove Term Limits for Elected City Officials
c.q: Shall Sections 37, and 56, of the Southgate City Charter be amended to eliminate term limits for the offices of Mayor, City Clerk, City Treasurer, and City Council?

c.title: CITY CHARTER AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE 5, GENERAL FINANCE, TO ESTABLISH BUDGET-BASED THRESHOLDS FOR COMPETITIVE BIDDING AND CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL ON PURCHASES, PUBLIC IMPROVEMENTS AND CONTRACTS
c.q: Shall the Charter of the City of Southgate be amended to require competitive bidding (sealed proposals) for City purchases, public improvements, and contracts that are 0.1% or more of the City’s annual operating budget; require City Council to establish annual thresholds for City Council approval of purchases, public improvements, and contracts; and provide that these thresholds may be adjusted each year by City Council Resolution when the City budget is adopted?

c.title: MILLAGE RENEWAL FOR BIKE PATH MAINTENANCE
c.q: Shall the expired previously voted increase in the total tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Grosse Ile Township, 0.15 mills ($0.15 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 0.1439 mills ($0.1439 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at 0.1439 mills ($0.1439 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for a period of ten (10) years from 2026 through 2035 inclusive, to provide funds for the maintenance of bike paths in the Township, raising an estimated $119,000 in the first calendar year the millage is levied of which a portion of the collection will be disbursed to the Grosse Ile Township Downtown Development Authority and the Brownfield Authority as legally required?

c.title: MILLAGE RENEWAL FOR FIRE DEPARTMENT EQUIPMENT
c.q: Shall the expired previously voted increase in the total tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Grosse Ile Township, of 0.50 mills ($0.50 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 0.4818 mills ($0.4818 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at 0.4818 mills ($0.4818 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for a period of 5 years from 2026 through 2030 inclusive, to provide funds for the acquiring of fire department vehicles and other necessary fire department equipment, raising an estimated $403,000 in the first calendar year the millage is levied (of which an estimated $5,750 will be disbursed to the Grosse Ile Township Downtown Development Authority and an estimated $1,800 to the Brownfield Authority as legally required)?

c.title: MILLAGE RENEWAL FOR RECREATION PROGRAM
c.q: Shall the expired previously voted increase in the total tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Grosse Ile Township, 0.50 mills ($0 .50 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to .4818 mills ($.4818 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at .4818 mills ($.4818 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for a period of five (5) years from 2026 through 2030 inclusive, to provide funds for the operation of a Township recreation program, raising an estimated $400,000 in the first calendar year the millage is levied of which a portion of the collection will be disbursed to the Grosse Ile Township Downtown Development Authority and the Brownfield Authority as legally required?

c.title: NEW MILLAGE FOR GREENWAYS/OPEN SPACE
c.q: Shall Grosse Ile Township impose an increase of up to 0.10 mill ($0.10 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the total tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for a period of 3 years, 2026 through 2028 inclusive, to provide funds for the purpose of maintenance and repair of public property and trails designated as greenways/open space properties, which 0.10 mill increase will raise an estimated $83,614 in the first year the millage is levied, of which a small portion will be disbursed to the Grosse Ile Township Downtown Development Authority and Brownfield Authority as legally required?

c.title: Redford Union School District
c.q:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.

Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Redford Union School District, Wayne County, Michigan, be increased by 12 mills ($12.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 5 years, 2026 to 2030, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2026 is approximately $225,346 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?

c.title: City of Dearborn Heights
c.pre: County of Wayne State of Michigan General Revision of the City Charter Proposal
c.q: Shall there be a general revision of the Charter of the City of Dearborn Heights?

c.title: Taylor School District
c.q:
This proposal, if approved by the electors, would, replace, restore and extend the authority of the School District to levy the statutory limit of 18 mills on all property, except principal residences and other property exempted by law, which currently expires with the School District’s 2027 tax levy and allow the School District to continue to levy the statutory limit of 18 mills in the event of future Headlee rollbacks required by the Michigan Constitution of up to 2 mills. The authorization will allow the School District to continue to receive revenues at the full per pupil foundation allowance permitted by the State.

Shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residences and other property exempted by law, situated within the Taylor School District, County of Wayne, State of Michigan, be increased, in the amount of 20 mills with 18 mills being the maximum allowable levy ($18.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation), for a period of ten (10) years, 2026 to 2035, inclusive, with 17.5603 mills of the above 20 mills being a replacement of authorized millage which will otherwise expire with the 2027 tax levy and 0.4397 mills being a restoration of previously authorized millage lost as a result of the rollbacks required by the Michigan Constitution? This operating millage if approved and levied, would provide estimated revenues to the School District of $420,661 during the 2026 calendar year, to be used for general operating purposes.

c.title: Dearborn Public Schools School Improvement Bond Proposition
c.q:
Shall the Dearborn Public Schools, County of Wayne, State of Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed One Billion Five Hundred Ten Million Dollars ($1,510,000,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds, in multiple series, to pay the cost of the following projects in order to implement the School District’s 2026 Facilities Master Plan which includes the construction of new preK-8 school buildings, major renovations at all school buildings including the three high schools, expanding space for career education programs, safety and security measures, improving infrastructure for STEAM programs, and traffic improvements:

Erecting and completing new school buildings and other facilities;

Remodeling, constructing additions to, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing, re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities;

Acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment in school buildings and other facilities; and

Preparing, developing and improving sites at school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities and the purchase of school buses?

The maximum number of years any series of bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of refunding, is not more than thirty (30) years; the estimated millage that will be levied to pay the proposed bonds in the first year is 3.14 mills (which is equal to $3.14 per $1,000 of taxable value); and the estimated simple average annual millage that will be required to retire each series of bonds is 5.67 mills annually ($5.67 per $1,000 of taxable value).

(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited, and the proceeds cannot be used for teacher, administrator or employee salaries, repair or maintenance costs or other operating expenses.)

c.title: Headlee Override Proposal
c.q:
Shall a “Headlee Override” be adopted so that the current limitation on the amount of City taxes that may be levied against all taxable property in the City of Lincoln Park, Wayne County, Michigan, be increased as follows:

Up to 20 mills from approximately 17.17 ($20.00 from approximately $17.17 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) for general operating expenses.

If approved and levied in its entirety, this millage would raise an estimated maximum amount of $2,420,265 for the City in 2027 by allowing the City to levy the maximum mills previously approved by the voters and authorized by the City Charter and State law which have been reduced as required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963.

c.title: Renewal of Schoolcraft College Operating Millage with continued Headlee Override
c.q: To renew the millage passed in 2018 for a ten (10) year period, shall the Schoolcraft Community College District, (consisting of the Clarenceville, Garden City, Livonia, Northville, Plymouth-Canton and part of the Novi public school districts) be authorized to continue levying this millage with Headlee override, which restored the 1986 voter-approved rate of 2.27 mills (about $2.27 per $1,000 of taxable valuation), which shall be assessed for ten (10) more years (2029 through 2038, inclusive), without further reduction by Section 31 of Article IX of the 1963 Michigan State Constitution, for operating purposes of Schoolcraft College. If approved, there would be no change in the current millage rate for the Schoolcraft Community College District. This renewal is estimated to generate $50,760,711 in 2029.
